title: 01 · RED by layer
description: Rate, Errors, Duration at each layer, following the request path: client -> LB -> api -> downstream -> async.

options.content: **Read top to bottom along the request path.** The first layer whose numbers drift is where to dig. The orange line on the charts is a change event (deploy, config). Commands: `make new` · `make hint` · `make answer`

panels.title: User requests/s by outcome
panels.description: Each logical user request, after retries. timeout and conn_error are errors only the client sees.

panels.title: Requests/s by tenant
panels.description: Workload characterization: who is causing the load?

panels.title: Attempts vs user requests
panels.description: When the two lines split, the client is retrying.

panels.title: 5xx at the LB vs 5xx api records itself
panels.description: Envoy counts the 503s it generates itself in upstream_rq_5xx, so compare with the errors api counts.

panels.title: Latency p99 and p99.9: LB vs api
panels.description: The gap between the LB and api is time spent in between: network, the queue ahead of the app, a process that stood still.

panels.title: Little's Law: measured in-flight vs rate × duration
panels.description: rate(sum of durations) = λ × W = L. The two lines should stay close.

panels.title: p99 success vs error (separately)
panels.description: Failed requests may be very fast (fail fast) or very slow (timeout).

panels.title: api latency heatmap (requests per bucket)
panels.description: The whole distribution over time. A band far above the main one is a tail; dots are exemplars to open in Tempo.

panels.title: DB session p99 (pool wait + connection held)
panels.description: The 'DB span' as the app sees it: includes the wait for a connection.

panels.title: Mean query time as seen from the app
panels.description: Excludes the pool wait. Compare with exec time in row 5.

panels.title: Calls to pricing: p99 as seen from api
Calls to pricing: new TCP connections/s vs calls/s
panels.description: With connection reuse, opens stay near 0 while calls flow. One open per call means every call pays a handshake.
